title: Lane Dash – Free Supermarket Runner Game (3 Lanes, Swipe to Play)
description: Play Lane Dash free in your browser: swipe your shopping cart between three lanes, jump boxes, duck under sale signs and grab turbo deals.
body: Push a cheerful shopping cart down endless supermarket aisles. Swipe left and right to switch lanes, swipe up to hop over boxes and swipe down to duck under hanging sale signs. One bump and the run is over.

Red deal tags give a short turbo that smashes through everything; green tags switch on a coin magnet. No text, runs of one to three minutes, and it plays well in portrait and landscape on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and desktops. Your best distance and your coins are saved automatically.
New here? Read how to play and the tips for longer runs.

title: How to Play Lane Dash – Swipe Controls, Obstacles and Deal Tags
description: Lane Dash controls: swipe left or right to change lane, up to jump, down to duck. Learn which obstacles to jump, duck or dodge, and what the deal tags do.
body: Your cart rolls forward by itself and keeps getting faster. On a phone or tablet, swipe anywhere on the screen. With a mouse, click and drag. On a keyboard, use the arrow keys or WASD (Space also jumps).
Left / right moves the cart one lane over. There are three lanes. Up jumps. Down ducks for a moment; if you are in the air, it drops you to the floor fast.

Each obstacle has one answer. Stacks of cardboard boxes are low: jump over them. Hanging sale signs are high: duck under them. Parked carts piled with shopping and yellow wet-floor signs are too tall to jump: change lane. When a whole row of boxes or signs blocks the aisle, jump or duck; when two lanes are blocked by carts or wet-floor signs, the free lane is the only way through.

Coins float above the floor in lines and arcs. Red deal tags (lightning bolt) give about three seconds of turbo: you go faster and knock obstacles out of the way. Green deal tags (magnet) pull nearby coins towards you for seven seconds.

Your score is the distance in metres, shown at the top. Coins are counted in the top left corner and add up across runs. If the portal offers it, you can watch an optional video once per run to keep going after a crash.

title: Lane Dash Tips: Run Further and Collect More Coins
description: Practical tips to beat your best distance in Lane Dash: look ahead, keep to the middle lane, jump late, save the turbo and use the magnet.
body: Look ahead, not at the cart. Rows appear far down the aisle. Decide on your lane while they are still small and you will never need a panic swipe.
Stay in the middle lane when you can. From the centre, both side lanes are one swipe away. From an edge lane, the far side takes two swipes.
Jump late. A jump lasts about half a second. Swipe up when the boxes are close, not when they first appear, or you will come down before you clear them.
Duck early. Ducking lasts a little longer than a jump, so you can swipe down as soon as the sign row is near.
Swipe down in the air to drop straight back to the floor. It saves you when a sign row comes right after a box row.
Follow the coins. Coin lines usually sit in a safe lane, and coin arcs show where to jump.
Turbo is a shield. While the turbo lasts you cannot crash, so pick the lane with the most coins and let the obstacles fly.
Short, clean swipes. One swipe is read as soon as your finger has moved a little, so you do not need long drags.

title: Lane Dash FAQ
description: Answers about Lane Dash: is it free, does it save, does it work in portrait, on mobile and Chromebook, and why did my cart crash.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser. There is nothing to buy.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Your best distance and your total coins are stored in your browser (on CrazyGames, in your account).
Does it work on phones, in portrait and on Chromebooks? Yes. It plays with touch, mouse or keyboard, in portrait or landscape. In tall screens the camera rises so you can see further down the aisle.
Why did my cart crash? You touched an obstacle. Boxes must be jumped, hanging signs must be ducked under, and parked carts and wet-floor signs can only be avoided by changing lane.
What do the red and green tags do? Red is a short turbo that makes you unstoppable; green is a coin magnet.
Is it a Subway Surfers copy? No. It uses the classic three-lane runner controls, but the setting, characters, obstacles, power-ups and art are our own.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button in the top right corner.

title: Lane Dash for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Lane Dash is a short, text-free runner game that works on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data.
h1: Lane Dash for classrooms and kids
body: Lane Dash has no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data. A run lasts one to three minutes, which makes it a good short reward between tasks.
There is no text in the game, so it works the same for children who are still learning to read and for students of any language.

It trains quick visual decisions: each obstacle has one correct answer (jump, duck or change lane), and the speed rises gently, so players practise reading what is coming and reacting calmly. Collecting coins adds a little counting.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and phones, in portrait or landscape, and loads in a couple of seconds (1.6 MB).
